subject: Dedicated performance validation: HW comparison & validation plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@mediqhealth.com>, Tom Raines <tom.raines@mediqhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated performance validation: HW comparison & validation plan

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed validation plan so we're all aligned on SLOs and what we need to validate on Dedicated capacity. I summarized the call highlights below and included proposed next steps & timeline.

Call highlights (as I captured them)
- Target workload: 100 rps steady-state (bursty up to ~160 rps), average output ~45 tokens, streaming responses required for UI (chunked streaming).
- Model: customer-managed Llama-2-13B finetune (fp16 checkpoint provided).
- Key SLOs: first-byte (streaming) P50 <= 120ms, first-byte P95 <= 350ms; end-to-end P95 <= 900ms for full responses; availability target 99.9%.
- Concurrency expectation: sustained concurrency ~40–60 active requests (depends on bursts).
- Cost sensitivity: want a price/throughput comparison to evaluate H100 vs A100 vs L40-class options.

Initial hardware/throughput tradeoffs (high level)
- H100 (best latency/throughput): lowest p95, handles higher concurrency with smaller instance counts; higher hourly cost. Strong for streaming and large-batch KV cache scenarios.
- A100 (mature, cost-effective): good balance for batch-heavy workloads; slightly higher p95 vs H100 at identical concurrency. Good fallback if H100 capacity limited.
- L40/L4 (inference-accelerator): cheaper per-hour; may require more nodes to hit throughput SLOs and can have slightly higher tail latency for long context sizes.

Proposed validation matrix (what we will run)
- Model variants: fp16 (customer checkpoint), int8/q4_0 (quantized variants we will produce with customer OK).
- Tests: cold KV vs warm KV; streaming-first-byte latency; steady-state throughput soak at 100 rps and 160 rps burst; incremental concurrency sweep (10, 25, 50, 75).
- Metrics: first-byte P50/P95, token throughput (tokens/s), cost-per-1M tokens estimate, memory utilization, percent of requests hitting fallback.
- Duration: 2 full soak days per hardware class (H100 / A100 / L40) + a short validation run for quantized variants.

Attachments: I attached the Mediq prompt set you mentioned (mediq-prompt-set-20270629.json) and a proposed benchmark matrix (benchmark-matrix-v1.xlsx). Please confirm these are the correct prompts we should use for quality gating.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Elena: please share a read-only link to the model artifact (or let us pull from your S3) and confirm permission to produce a quantized copy.
2) Mediq: confirm preferred 2-day windows (we're proposing Jul 7–8 or Jul 12–13) and whether you want H100 prioritized.
3) Internal: Ben / Lauren — can you confirm capacity to schedule H100 nodes for two full validation days and estimate cost delta for H100 vs A100 vs L40?

Ballpark pricing (very rough):
- Dedicated baseline (reserved): 2x H100 equivalent reserved capacity recommended to meet steady-state w/ buffer — we'll follow up with firm numbers after the validation run.

I'll consolidate results and proposed Dedicated configs after the runs. Thanks — should be a straightforward validation if we get the artifact access and time windows confirmed.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 10:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (recap omitted)

Thanks Soojin — good summary. A few internal notes / asks from infra side before we confirm windows:

1) H100 scheduling: I can reserve an H100 pool for Jul 7–8 (2 days) but need confirmation by EOD Wednesday (Jun 30) so we can lock capacity. If Mediq prefers Jul 12–13 instead, we can try but there is slightly higher risk of contention.

2) Benchmark matrix updates: I'll add explicit batch-size sweep (1, 2, 4, 8) and streaming chunk sizes (16, 32, 64 tokens) to the spreadsheet. Also will add a "cold-start" row where we wipe KV cache every 5 minutes to measure cold tail.

3) Quantization plan: we need explicit written approval to produce q4_0 and int8 candidate builds. If they approve, we'll generate quantized images and run a short quality check of 200 prompt samples from the prompt-set to validate hallucination/regression risk.

4) Cost delta estimate (very rough): per-hour comparative headroom: H100 ~ 1.6x cost vs A100; L40 ~ 0.45x cost vs A100 for basic inference; net effective tokens/sec and p95 will determine the final recommendation. I'll provide a more concrete cost/throughput table after first validation runs.

Action items (assignments):
- Ben: lock H100 nodes pending confirmation; update benchmark spreadsheet and include exact metrics columns.
- Lauren: prepare a short evaluation checklist for quality gating on quantized builds.
- Soojin: push the PO / timeline decision with Mediq and get model access.

Will follow up with an updated benchmark-matrix before EOD.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Elena / Tom — great, thanks for the fast turnaround. Jul 12–13 works and we've tentatively reserved H100 capacity for those dates pending Ben's capacity lock (Ben: please confirm by EOD).

Summary of confirmed decisions:
- Access: Redwood team will use the Mediq test S3 bucket: s3://mediq-models/prod/llama2-13b-fin/202706 (read-only).
- Quantization: Mediq approved q4_0 and int8 artifacts for validation; Redwood will write quantized builds to a Redwood-managed test bucket.
- Test window: Jul 12–13 (2 full soak days).
- Acceptance gating: we will run the 200-sample quality check on quantized builds; if quality deltas exceed agreed thresholds (to be added to the benchmark-matrix), we will not recommend quantized for Dedicated.

Next steps / deliverables
1) Ben: post updated benchmark-matrix (with batch/stream chunk sweeps) and a cost/throughput estimate table by EOD Jun 30.
2) Lauren: draft the 200-sample quality checklist by Jul 6.
3) Soojin: circulate a short mutual-action plan for procurement milestones and expected deliverable dates (I'll include drive links and the hubspot deal id).

I'll send a calendar invite for a short kickoff on Jul 9 to walk through the validation run plan and expectations. Thanks all — looking forward to the runs.
